settings.heading: Two actives. Thirty millilitres. Nothing else competing for the space.

settings.text: Most serums pad a long ingredient list to look impressive. This one is built on NAD and collagen extract, in a glass dropper that lets you see exactly what you are using.

NAD — nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide — is a coenzyme found in every living cell, and the active this serum is named for.

Collagen extract works at the surface: it helps the formula spread evenly and leaves skin feeling conditioned rather than tight. It does not build collagen from the outside — no topical does, and any page telling you otherwise is one search away from being found out.

settings.heading: Description
settings.row_content:
A firming serum built on two actives — NAD and collagen extract — in a 30 ml / 1 fl oz glass dropper bottle.

The texture is deliberately light. Two to three drops sink in within seconds and sit under moisturiser and SPF without pilling, so it slots into a routine you already have rather than replacing it.

This is a cosmetic product, formulated to improve the look and feel of skin rather than to treat any skin condition.

settings.heading: How To Apply
settings.row_content:
Two to three drops on clean skin, morning and night. Press it in rather than rubbing, give it about a minute to absorb, then moisturiser — and SPF in the morning.

More is not better. The dropper is there so you can be exact; over-applying is the usual reason a serum pills under everything else.

settings.heading: Layering With Other Actives
settings.row_content: Most people alternate rather than stack: vitamin C in the morning, retinol at night, this serum in either. If you want all three, introduce them one at a time so you can tell what your skin is responding to.

settings.heading: Suitability & Patch Testing
settings.row_content:
Suits normal, combination and dry skin. Patch test before the first full application — a little on the inner forearm, left 24 hours. Avoid the eye area and stop if your skin becomes irritated.

If you are pregnant, breastfeeding or under the care of a dermatologist, check before adding anything new to your routine.

settings.heading: Storage & Bottle Life
settings.row_content:
Store upright somewhere cool and dry, out of direct sunlight. The tinted glass helps keep light off the formula, but a sunny windowsill will still undo that.

At two to three drops twice a day, a 30 ml bottle is a long run — which is the argument for a dropper over a pump: you can see what you are using.

settings.heading: Shipping
settings.row_content:
Most orders arrive 15–30 days from the day you order, tracked the whole way. We pack and dispatch within 1–2 business days.

The bottle is glass and travels boxed and padded. If yours arrives damaged, send a photo and we replace it.

Refunds go back to your original payment method within 5–10 business days of us receiving the return.

settings.title: Complete The Routine
settings.description: The serum is one step. These are the ones either side of it — the cleanse before, and the moisturiser that seals it in.

settings.text:
Skin changes slowly and photographs badly. The fair test is not the mirror on day three — it is whether your skin feels less tight after cleansing, whether makeup sits better on it, and whether you notice something at week four that you did not at week one.

Take a photo on day one, in the same light you will use for the next one. It is the only comparison worth trusting, and almost nobody thinks to do it before they start.
